Zo bereid: Opening en context Ons onderz: Get ready: Opening and context Our research predicts that the Circular Plastics NL subsidy will likely open on 6 October 2026 with a budget of approximately €40 million. Treat this as an important lead: deadlines and limited resources make quick, focused preparation necessary. The underlying problem is concrete for many plastic recycling companies: a lack of capital to finance innovative upscaling. Use this signal to force strategic choices, not to sow panic.
1) Signaal → context: bevestig en priori: 1) Signal → context: confirm and prioritize - What to do: put the expected opening date and an internal deadline calendar entry (at least 1 week before the external deadline) in the diary. Name who owns the application. - Ownership: CEO/owner or project manager (subsidy project owner). - Measure: calendar appointment + project owner named within 48 hours. - Why: without rapid ownership the application stalls and you lose time for partners and co-financing.
2) Gevolg → besluit: bepaal strategische: 2) Consequence → decision: determine strategic fit - Signal translated to business context: which projects in your roadmap require investment for scaling (e.g. new washing lines, sorting technology, compounding)? Which fit within the subsidy rules? - Decision: will you submit a subsidy application for (A) one concrete scale project, (B) multiple projects, or (C) not apply and seek alternative financing? - Ownership: executive team during a short decision moment. - Measure: go/no-go decision within 5 working days; chosen project and scope documented.
3) Actieplan (stap‑voor‑stap uitvoering): 3) Action plan (step-by-step execution) Follow this checklist as an operational action plan. Each item names an owner and a verifiable result.
4) Resultaat → meten Voor iedere ingedie: 4) Result → measure For each submitted application set concrete metrics: - Completeness: all required attachments present (yes/no). - Financial trail: co-financing demonstrable (%) and intentions recorded. - Project KPIs: target tonnes recycled per year, quality level (e.g. % PCR material) or throughput time reduction — choose 1–2 that are demonstrably monitorable. - Ownership: who monitors progress after submission (project owner).
5) Leren → gesloten lus Na indiening of: 5) Learn → closed loop After submission or outcome conduct a short review: - What went well/what could be better? What took too long? Which documents did we miss? - Make standard improvements: budget template, standard partner letter of intent, checklist for technical documentation. - Measure: improvement plan ready within 7 days after outcome; assigned owner for implementation.

Vergelijking tussen de huidige situatie: Comparison between the current situation and the situation with this preparation: what changes for you?
Stap A — Projectcase & ambities (2–5 dag: Step A — Projectcase & ambitions (2–5 days) - Action: describe the problem, solution, desired scaling speed, expected investment amount and exactly what the subsidy should cover. - Owner: project manager. - Metric: one‑page projectcase ready and approved by CEO.
Stap B — Financiële readiness (3–7 dagen: Step B — Financial readiness (3–7 days) - Action: create a project budget with total costs, requested subsidy amount and concrete co‑financing (own funds, loan, partner contribution). Subsidies often have co‑financing requirements; show where the rest of the budget comes from. - Owner: CFO / financial responsible. - Metric: budget + letter of intent from co‑financer(s) or internal funds secured. - Hypothetical example (one clarification): suppose you are Petra, owner of recycling company “GroenPlast”. Your projectcase requests €500.000 for an additional extrusion line. For the application you fill in: requested subsidy €300.000; own funds €100.000; investment loan under the bank's intent €100.000 (written intent). This letter of intent makes your budget plausible for reviewers.
Stap C — Technische en regelgevingstoets: Step C — Technical and regulatory assessment (4–10 days) - Action: describe technical specifications, output quality of the recycled material, quality controls and environmental/regulatory compliance (e.g. traceability of plastic streams). Add a simple Gantt with execution times. - Owner: technical lead / operations. - Metric: technical document and schedule ready; risk points and mitigations identified.
Stap D — Partners & keten (7–14 dagen) -: Step D — Partners & supply chain (7–14 days) - Action: delineate chain partners (raw material suppliers, customers, research institutions, local government) and request short letters of intent or partnership statements. - Owner: business development / partnerships. - Metric: at least one partnership with a letter of intent in the application (more is better), partners list with contact details.
Stap E — Aanvraagtekst & bijlagen (3–7 d: Step E — Application text & attachments (3–7 days) - Action: complete the application with clear objectives, KPIs and attachments (budget, letters of intent, technical documents, timeline). - Owner: subsidy project owner + writer (can be internal or external). - Metric: draft application complete; internal review and checklist completed.
Stap F — Kwaliteitscontrole en inleveren: Step F — Quality control and submission (1–3 days) - Action: run a four‑eyes review: completeness, budget alignment and signing; upload/submit according to portal requirements. - Owner: project owner + CEO for final sign‑off. - Metric: proof of submission or timely upload; backup (PDF) saved.
Risico’s en mitigaties - Risico: onvoldo: Risks and mitigations - Risk: insufficient co‑financing.
Mitigatie: start vroeg gesprekken met ba: Mitigation: start early conversations with banks and partners, and create multiple financing scenarios. - Risk: missing technical data. Mitigation: allow time for an external technical review or collaboration with a knowledge institution. - Risk: deadline miscalculation. Mitigation: internal deadline at least 7 working days before the final date.
Praktische tips - Werk met vaste documen: Practical tips - Work with fixed documents: a one-page project case, one core budget, and one partner template. That speeds up iterations. - Appoint a short sprint: a 90‑min kickoff with the CEO, finance and the technical lead shortens decision-making and delivers clarity within 48 hours. - Keep decision criteria simple: for the reviewer one paragraph should explain why the project is scalable, measurable and sustainable.
Slotadvies Behandel een voorspelde subsi: Final advice Treat a predicted subsidy notification as an urgent opportunity: rapid ownership, a concise project case and demonstrable co‑financing are decisive. Start today by naming a project owner, plan the 90‑min kickoff and complete the one-page project case within five working days. This turns the signal into a controlled action with a measurable outcome.
